# Galpi

> Galpi (갈피) is an open-source, experimental navigation layer that keeps AI coding agents such as Claude Code and OpenAI Codex from getting lost in a codebase. It improves code structure first, then adds a compact machine-readable index (`.gp` files) only for what code cannot express: task state (done, WIP, plan, dead, locked), intent, and routing from a task alias to the minimal set of files. Every design decision is measured on both agents before adoption, and refuted claims stay in the record. Apache-2.0 (code) and CC BY 4.0 (experiment data, spec), by Jason (@jasonwpgml).

Key facts:
- Entry point for agents: `galpi-lab/.galpi/BOOT.gp` and `galpi-lab/.galpi/MAP.gp`, read together; `galpi-lab/AGENTS.md` is a 3-line bootstrap pointing to them. Human docs (README, docs/) are not default agent context.
- Navigation order: BOOT + MAP, then route(alias), then task view `.galpi/v/t/<task>.gp`, then only the files that view lists. No repository-wide search when the route hits.
- State codes: 0 done, 1 wip, 2 plan, 3 exp, 4 dead, 5 stale, h hot, l lock. Dead and locked paths are blocked by a PreToolUse hook (exit 2), pre-commit and CI, not by prompt compliance.
- Scale-adaptive depth L0 to L3: L0 is structure rules plus a few lines of AGENTS.md and no `.galpi` at all; the index is added only when a project is large enough to repay its bootstrap cost.
- CLI (TypeScript, Node.js 20+): `galpi check` (contract validation, exit 1 on violation), `galpi doctor` (structural diagnostics), `galpi build` (code graph manifest), `galpi query <alias>` (minimal files, symbols and dependencies), plus mutation commands with schema validation and byte-level rollback.
- Measured on Codex: compact `.gp` index vs verbose human-readable docs cut total tokens 16.6% (C2) and 20.3% (C3), with state-rule compliance up to 100%.
- Measured on Claude Code: explicit rules fixed accuracy (100%) but cost +12.1% tokens; moving enforcement into a PreToolUse hook cut that to +1.9%, with effective tokens -1.3% and cost -2.8%.
- Phase 3.5 (2x2, 96 runs, both agents): improved structure alone was the cheapest condition; the index cut code read by 63 to 78% but raised total tokens on a 1,300-line fixture because of bootstrap turns. Unconditional "always add an index" was withdrawn.
- Raw run logs are not published; the write-ups are the record. The experiment runner is included.
- Spec: `GALPI_SPEC_v0.2_draft.md` is a draft L3 (multi-agent collaboration) packet protocol, v0.x, breaking changes possible.
